summary: Split-horizon SRV priority/weight oscillation pins gRPC streams to an unhealthy AZ causing intermittent 524s and model shard download stalls
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 524 gateway timeouts and stalled model shard downloads from serving nodes in eu-west after we provisioned their private deployment. Impact: Serving requests intermittently hang for 20-90s and return 524 or gRPC CANCELLED before succeeding on retry. Affects user-facing inference and batch artifact fetches. Environment: Private deployment over transit VPC (customer-managed peering) with split-horizon DNS; control plane endpoints are resolved via customer's internal resolver for serving nodes and via public resolver for control-plane health checks. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a large model request that requires shard downloads (e.g., 200MB ranges). 2) Observe gRPC stream establishment and subsequent 20-90s stalls followed by 524 or CANCELLED. 3) Repeat; behavior is intermittent and correlates with SRV record changes in customer DNS. Observed behavior: gRPC channels are repeatedly anchored to a single AZ's serving nodes that are intermittently degraded; DNS SRV responses from customer resolver reorder priority and weight between responses (split-horizon + low TTL). Expected behavior: SRV responses should present stable ordering/weights or our client should round-robin across healthy endpoints; gRPC should failover more quickly. Relevant logs: "stream_id=0x1a3c connect_to=svc-azb.eu-west-1.redwood.svc:443 delay=27.8s err=GRPC_CANCELLED"; DNS trace: ";; ANSWER SECTION: _redwood._tcp.redwood.svc 30 IN SRV 10 50 443 svc-aza...\n;; ANSWER SECTION: _redwood._tcp.redwood.svc 30 IN SRV 5 100 443 svc-azb..." Additional context: Customer runs an internal DNS layer that performs health-aware SRV rewriting and has a short TTL (30s). Their resolver sometimes returns the same SRV set with different priority/weight ordering across sequential queries which appears to interact with our client-side SRV selection and gRPC channel pinning logic.

investigation: Initial triage combined customer-provided packet captures, DNS traces, and server-side metrics. Evidence: 1) DNS traces show SRV sets with identical targets but varying priority/weight between sequential queries. 2) gRPC client logs indicate channels are established to the first backend in the SRV set and kept alive across requests (channel pinning). 3) Serving node metrics show elevated request queue times in eu-west-1-b during incidents. 4) Customer firewall logs show sporadic egress queueing and SYN delays impacting one AZ. Conclusion: root cause is a combination of customer-side split-horizon DNS reordering (low TTL + health-aware rewriting) and a client-side SRV selection implementation that prefers ordered SRV entries and pins channels, which amplifies transient AZ-level network degradations into sustained request stalls.
resolution: Short-term mitigation: Instructed customer to enable SRV shuffle on their internal resolver (applied 2026-03-11 20:10 UTC) and to increase SRV TTL to 60s. We released a server-side client config change to randomize SRV selection and reduce channel pin lifetime (infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4021) as a mitigant for private deployments behind split-horizon resolvers. Long-term: Engineering will land a robust SRV failover strategy in the client library that: 1) randomizes (or respects weight) SRV selection if TTL < 60s, 2) refreshes pinned endpoints after a short backoff on repeated errors, and 3) surfaces per-AZ health in tracing for faster detection. Follow-ups: INT task to add SRV-ordering test cases (INT-2041), update Private Deployment runbook with DNS guidance, and schedule a postmortem with the customer in 1 week.
